results.corrected_extracted: Gastrointestinal effects in 36 (51%): vomiting 31, nausea alone 5. Tachycardia in 27 (38%; no threshold stated) and systolic blood pressure above 140 mmHg in 32 (45%). Median stay 16 hours (IQR 11.3–24.4; range 1.8–228). Eight (11%), all of whom had taken tramadol with another medicine, went to intensive care: 5 for the other medicines' toxicity (tricyclic antidepressants 3, morphine 1, atenolol 1) and 3 for respiratory depression (one intubated, one on a naloxone infusion, one who developed pneumonia). No deaths. Naloxone was given to 9, seven with documented respiratory depression: it was reported to improve oxygen saturation or consciousness in 6, to improve them partly in 2 and to have no effect in 1; no seizures were reported after it.
results.note: Every number matches. Wording only: the paper says naloxone 'was reported to improve' (response taken from the medical record, Methods 4th paragraph) and that one ICU patient 'developed pneumonia'.

results.corrected_extracted: The authors say serotonin toxicity reported after therapeutic use or overdose of tramadol has been with other medicines given with it, particularly serotonergic antidepressants (1st paragraph); later they say the majority of reported cases involved co-ingested serotonergic drugs and only one unusual severe case has been described (5th paragraph). Their concluding paragraph takes the absence of serotonin toxicity in these overdoses as suggesting that at therapeutic doses tramadol is unlikely to cause more than minor serotonergic effects, although nobody taking therapeutic doses, alone or with antidepressants, was studied.
results.note: Paragraph count confirmed. The 5th paragraph says 'the majority of cases'; 'without them' is implied there, not stated. The conclusion is hedged ('suggesting'). No numbers changed.

Discussion 2nd, 3rd and 7th paragraphs match each part: 8% and 14%, 35% and 46%, 132 of 215, 'greater than 2000 mg' against the Results' '2000 mg or higher dose', Talaie's 500-1000 mg, and the limitations.

results.corrected_extracted: Background: much of the toxicity in tramadol overdose is thought to be due to monoamine uptake inhibition rather than its opioid effects (citing Spiller et al., a prospective multicentre evaluation of tramadol exposures); and, citing a review of tramadol's clinical pharmacology, tramadol is metabolised by CYP2D6 to O-desmethyltramadol, a more potent μ-receptor agonist with a longer half-life (9 hours against 6 for tramadol), which contributes to tramadol's duration and analgesic potency.
results.note: Attribution: the toxicity sentence cites ref. 3 (Spiller et al. 1997, a prospective multicentre study), not the review (ref. 1, Grond and Sablotzki), which supports only the CYP2D6 sentence. 'Liver' is not in the source.

key_findings.correction: Median length of stay 16 hours (IQR 11.3–24.4, range 1.8–228); 19.9 hours (IQR 13.6–35.7) after co-ingestion. 8 patients (11%), all of whom had taken other medicines, went to intensive care: 5 for co-ingestant toxicity (tricyclic antidepressants 3, morphine 1, atenolol 1) and 3 for respiratory depression (one intubated, one on a naloxone infusion, one who developed pneumonia). No deaths. Naloxone was given to 9 patients, 7 with documented respiratory depression; it was reported to improve oxygen saturation or consciousness in 6, to improve them partly in 2 and to have no effect in 1; no seizures were reported after naloxone.

reporting_issues.correction: issue: The amount comparison between patients with and without seizures is given p=0.018 in the Results (p. 3) and p=0.021 in the Figure 1 legend (p. 4). | consequence: Minor; the direction is unaffected. The paper does not explain the difference, which may be a transcription error or a different computation (for example exact against approximate Mann–Whitney p).

risk_of_bias.note: Moderate fits: complete prospective case capture and pre-defined outcomes, against one centre, self-reported amounts without laboratory confirmation, 72% co-ingestion and few events. Design (case series) and instrument (JBI prevalence) also agreed.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor: frequencies are reported faithfully; the title's 'causes' and the conclusion's extension to therapeutic doses (hedged 'suggesting') sit at the upper end of minor.

missed: Figure 1 (PDF p. 4), measured on a 600-dpi rendering: the no-seizure group's central bar sits at about 1,400 mg with whiskers at about 350 and 2,470 mg, not at the text's median 1,000 mg (IQR 775–1,550 mg), although the legend says the bars are median and IQR; a figure–text inconsistency (the seizure group's centre, about 2,100 mg, matches).

The authors' stated hypothesis was that serotonin toxicity would occur with tramadol overdose and that seizures and coma would be the most important effects (PDF p. 2, Introduction, last paragraph); the serotonin finding ran against their own hypothesis.
